problems.scenario: 1. Solo GP who is doctor, receptionist and cashier at once (Billing on)
problems.detail: Rows: organizations(1); departments: one row 'Clinic' (core type, no Reception row is needed because roles are global: user_roles.department_id NULL = everywhere); users: one staff row made by create_organization (service_role) and linked by link_login; user_roles: (gp, owner, NULL), (gp, doctor, NULL), (gp, receptionist, NULL), (gp, cashier, NULL). The owner holds manage:*, so MFA must be enrolled before first-run setup; recovery is the developer unenrolling in the dashboard (decided, but for a solo practice the developer is the only recovery). Clinical trace: write_note(patient, department_id = Clinic) -> require_access(org, 'write:note', patient, Clinic) finds (doctor, NULL) -> write_entry -> one pack_calls(billing, entry_id, org) row -> COMMIT. Runner tick: set_config('opencare.acting_user_id', <org's 'pack:billing' user>) -> billing.after_write(entry) inserts billing.charges. For a request (HbA1c to an outside lab) after_write calls mark_step(id, 'sent', 'held'): (a) the pack role's grant list names read_…, core.write_entry, core.change_request and the gates, but not public.mark_step, so the call is refused at the grant; (b) if granted, require_access(org, 'mark:held', patient, to_department_id) looks for a user_roles row of the 'pack:billing' user, and nothing in the design creates that user or gives it a role. Either way error_text is written, tries reaches five, and every request in the practice is parked on the Organization page with Retry. Release path is fine: billing_mark_paid -> mark_step(id, 'held', 'sent') gated on mark:sent held by cashier everywhere. Everything else about one person holding four roles in one department works: one department, four link rows, one screen.
problems.fix: Two rules, no columns: (1) the pack role grant list adds EXECUTE on public.mark_step and public.mark_routing; (2) switching a pack on creates the organization's 'pack:<pack>' users row (kind = 'machine') and one user_roles row for the pack's built-in role (roles.organization_id IS NULL, key = pack key, shipped by the pack migration) with department_id NULL; switching off retires that user.

problems.scenario: 2. First-run setup from the 'Internal medicine clinic' preset, heavy edits, then a release ships an improved preset
problems.detail: Presets are client-shipped data (tables rejected). Flow: sign up -> MFA -> create_organization (service_role) returns the owner users row -> the client calls save_department x3 (Reception, Internal medicine, Laboratory if the pack is on), served_departments rows (Reception -> clinic), save_service x~60 each with service_fields, save_template x~5; every call passes require_access(org, 'manage:…', NULL, department) with the owner's NULL-scoped role and writes settings_changes. Failure point: the network drops at call 37. If save_… ids are minted by the server, re-running the preset creates a second 'CBC' in the same department; nothing refuses it because a same-code service is treated as a 'second provider' prompt, not a duplicate. If ids are client-minted UUIDv7 (as entries are) and save_ upserts by id, the re-run is idempotent, but the design does not say which. Second gap: preset services carry 'loinc:' codes; codes.code is the primary key with organization_id NULL for global rows, unit and kind set once, and nothing says who inserts global rows. If save_service creates them on first use, the first organization on a shared database fixes the unit of loinc:718-7 for every later organization (a cross-organization side effect); if nobody creates them, the preset fails on the first field. Heavy edits: in place, recorded in settings_changes; nothing points at a preset, so the improved preset in the next release changes nothing in existing organizations, which is correct. Built-in roles, department_types and entry_types arrive by migration and change everywhere at once; that is the only release channel into a live organization and should be said.
problems.fix: Two rules: save_… functions take a client-minted UUIDv7 id and upsert on it, so setup and imports are re-runnable; global codes rows (organization_id IS NULL) are written only by _core_ migrations, and save_service refuses a non-local code that is not in codes. Add UNIQUE (organization_id, department_id, code) WHERE retired_at IS NULL on services so a re-run can never make two CBCs in one department.

problems.scenario: 3. Adding a second lab mid-year where both offer CBC; served_departments left incomplete
problems.detail: Admin: save_department('ER lab', type 'laboratory') -> require_pack(org, 'laboratory'); save_service(ER lab, code loinc:58410-2, 'CBC', reply_type values, fields…). The save-time check finds a live service with the same (organization_id, code) in the main lab and the client prompts 'which departments does ER lab serve?' -> served_departments(ER lab -> ER). The main lab, having been the sole provider, has no served rows. Now an ER doctor picking CBC sees two providers; ER lab serves ER so it is the default. A ward doctor sees two providers and neither serves the ward, so the picker forces a choice on every request; the admin must add main lab -> each of the other 38 departments, and again for every department created later. If served_departments is left empty nothing is lost: requests still carry to_department_id = the chosen service's department, the queue index is untouched, open requests keep their destination, and entry_values trend by code across both labs. Templates hold service ids, so the 'ER panel' template made before the ER lab existed silently keeps sending CBC to the main lab until someone edits it; nothing tells the admin which templates name the other provider.
problems.fix: One convention using the pattern user_roles already uses: served_departments.served_department_id NULL means every department. The second-provider prompt then has one answer for the main lab, new departments need nothing, and 'a practice with one lab never touches it' stays true. The client lists the templates naming the other provider when the prompt fires.

problems.scenario: 4. An ER lab that covers the main lab after hours
problems.detail: Nothing in the design has a schedule; served_departments is static, so after 22:00 a ward CBC still defaults to the main lab and lands in requests with to_department_id = main lab. The only path is membership: the night technician holds user_roles (technician, main lab) and (technician, ER lab). She opens read_queue(main lab) (gate passes on main lab), calls laboratory_mark_collected([ids], specimen_no, occurred_at) (gate per request on requests.to_department_id = main lab), runs the sample on the ER analyser, and the analyser's machine users row writes the result as a reply: entries.department_id must be non-null for source machine, so it is the ER lab; the reply to a main-lab request from an ER-lab entry is not refused anywhere in spec 01; change_request closes the request. Works. Awkward: turnaround reports show the main lab's queue; the alternative (mark_routing each request to the ER lab) needs mark:routing in the main lab and a click per request; two labs means two CBC service rows with two sets of ranges to maintain, which is correct for two analysers but doubles the settings work.
problems.fix: State the rule, no schema: cover is membership; the covering staff hold roles in the covered department, the request stays where it was sent, and the reply's department_id says who did it.

problems.scenario: 6. A one-week locum
problems.detail: save_user(kind 'staff', name, title) makes the row, which is the invitation; user_roles (locum, doctor, clinic); link_login(user_id, auth id) links the login. link_login is executable by service_role only and the admin's client never holds service_role, so the design has no named caller for it (Edge Functions were rejected, claim by e-mail was rejected): the invite path is unspecified. Her entries carry author_id = her users row; her replies set review_needed_at on requests with requester_id = her. Day 7: the admin sets retired_at; every public function starts with require_access, which refuses a retired user on the next call regardless of JWT lifetime; her unreviewed results are owned by the department via read_to_review(org, clinic) and the second partial index (from_department_id, review_needed_at). Next year: save_user clears retired_at (the one un-retire). The convention 'retire on the day' is the weak point: a forgotten locum keeps full access, and there is no end date by decision.
problems.fix: A rule, not a column: save_user may set retired_at in the future and the gate refuses when retired_at <= now(); the admin retires Friday 18:00 on Monday. Name one server-side caller of link_login (one Edge Function 'invite' that calls auth.admin.inviteUserByEmail then link_login).

problems.scenario: 8. A doctor leaving with 30 open requests assigned and 12 results to review
problems.detail: Retire: save_user sets retired_at; the gate refuses her next call. The 30 open requests: requests.assignee_id = her in some to_department; read_queue(department) returns assignee_id, the client filters 'assigned to (retired)', and a colleague with mark:routing there calls mark_routing(request_id, assignee_id = other) thirty times (one screen action, thirty calls; no bulk function by decision). The 12 results: requests.requester_id = her, review_needed_at set; read_to_review(org, her clinic) via the (from_department_id, review_needed_at) index shows them to anyone holding mark:reviewed there; mark_reviewed gates on from_department_id. Replies that arrive later to her still-open requests set review_needed_at and appear in the same department list. Personal templates (templates.user_id) stay. Nothing is lost. What is awkward: retiring is silent; nobody is told that 30 assignments and 12 reviews are now orphaned, and the queue shows them only if someone thinks to filter by a retired assignee.
problems.fix: save_user returning {open_assigned, to_review} counts when it retires a user (a return value, no schema), so the client can say 'reassign 30, 12 results now owned by Internal medicine'.

problems.scenario: 9. Retiring a department that has years of history and 4 open requests
problems.detail: retire_department(id): counts requests WHERE to_department_id = id AND status = 'open' (the queue index) = 4 -> raises department_has_open_requests, as spec 01 says (open includes held and reopened). The admin reroutes each with mark_routing(to_department_id = other) or the requesters cancel, then retries; the call sets retired_at on the department and its services together. History: entries carry department_name and to_department_name in data; done requests keep to_department_id pointing at the retired row; templates naming its services are skipped on apply. Gaps: (a) user_roles rows with that department and served_departments rows naming it are neither deleted nor said to be ignored; a doctor whose only role is in the retired department must be refused, and a served row must not keep making the retired lab a default; (b) requests with from_department_id = id and review_needed_at set (results its doctors have not yet reviewed) are not counted; after retirement nobody holds mark:reviewed there, read_to_review(org, id) is refused, and a critical result waits on one person noticing it in 'mine'.
problems.fix: One more clause in retire_department: refuse while EXISTS (requests WHERE from_department_id = id AND review_needed_at IS NOT NULL) (the second partial index answers it), and delete the department's user_roles and served_departments rows in the same call.

problems.scenario: 11. Changing a reference range
problems.detail: save_service(id, fields[…reference_low/high…]) updates service_fields in place and writes settings_changes. Flags are computed once: history keeps its copied ranges and flags; a result written after the save copies the new range server-side in write_entry step 5, so a technician whose form was open before the change still gets the range in force at write time; an analyser result (source machine) keeps its own range and flag as given. Two things are unclear. (a) Sex- and age-specific ranges: the decision says service_field_ranges ships 'with the Laboratory pack', but write_entry (core) must read it to flag a value, and core never joins a pack schema; if it lands in schema laboratory the extraction cannot see it and every Hb is flagged on a unisex range for good. (b) Whether a range change is an in-place update or retire-and-insert of the field row is not said; in place is right (settings history is settings_changes, not row versions), but the position primary key makes retire-and-insert ambiguous.
problems.fix: State that service_field_ranges (service_id, position, sex, age_low, age_high, reference_low/high, critical_low/high) is a core table in a _core_ migration released with the Laboratory pack, read only through field_range(field, patient) in write_entry step 5, and that range edits are in-place updates recorded in settings_changes.

problems.scenario: 12. Moving a service from one department to another
problems.detail: Nothing says whether services.department_id may change. If save_service updates it in place: new requests copy the new department into requests.to_department_id at send time (spec 01: to_department_id = services.department_id at send), open requests keep their old destination and old queue, entries keep the composite FK (organization_id, service_id) and their copied names, templates keep the id and keep working, and the second-provider check fires if the target department already has that code. The open requests at the old department need mark_routing one by one, or they finish where they are. If instead the rule were retire-and-recreate, every template naming the old id starts skipping it, trends still work (by code) but the picker shows two rows for months. The in-place move is strictly better and needs one sentence.
problems.fix: One rule: services.department_id may change through save_service; open requests keep their destination and are rerouted with mark_routing if wanted; a move into a department that already offers the code is refused like a duplicate.

problems.scenario: 13. A shared reception feeding three clinics
problems.detail: Rows: departments Reception (type reception), A, B, C; served_departments (Reception -> A), (Reception -> B), (Reception -> C); receptionists hold user_roles (receptionist, Reception) only. Registering a patient and starting a visit (spec 03 functions) gate on Reception, fine. The doctor picker 'uses write:note in that department': the receptionist reads the users holding write:note in clinic A and reads A's patient queue, but the gate is require_access(org, action, patient, A) and she holds nothing in A, so every such read is refused unless served_departments is consulted somewhere, and the design says only that served_departments 'homes reception'. Giving receptionists a role in A, B and C instead would work but contradicts 'reception is tied to the clinics it feeds' and leaks whatever else that role holds.
problems.fix: One gate clause, narrow: the reads a serving department needs (the staff list and the patient queue of a served department) accept the serving department as department_id and pass when served_departments(caller's department, target) exists; no other action is widened.

problems.scenario: 14. An outside referral hospital and an outside reference lab
problems.detail: services 'Referral' and 'HbA1c (send-out)' have department_id NULL = outside; write_request names the destination at send time and creates the departments row (is_outside true, contact_text) on first use without manage:departments, which is what spec 01 says; requests.to_department_id points at it and the composite FK holds. The reply comes back as an entry with source outside, written by a clerk in the requesting clinic (department_id = clinic; flags and unit kept as given), and change_request closes the request. Nobody can hold a role in an outside department, so no step is ever marked there; cancel belongs to the requester. The operational hole: 'what did we send to the reference lab this month that has not come back' is read_queue(outside department), gated on a department where nobody holds read:queue, and read_sent_outside is deferred to spec 03; until then a lost send-out is found only per patient. Also nothing refuses a user_roles row on an outside department.
problems.fix: One gate clause now: read:queue on a department with is_outside passes for anyone holding read:queue in any department of the organization; and a CHECK-by-trigger that user_roles never names an outside department.

problems.scenario: 15. A branch site
problems.detail: departments North reception, North clinic, North lab, North ward with site_name 'North'; served_departments (North reception -> North clinic), (North lab -> North clinic), (North lab -> North ward), main lab -> everyone (needs the NULL convention from scenario 3, otherwise a row per department); a doctor working both sites has two user_roles rows; patients and the record are organization-wide, so a North visit reads the same record; the queue is per department so nothing crosses sites by accident; Billing's cash desk per site is the pack's own settings. What strains is the label: site_name is free text, 'Nort h' makes a phantom site in every site filter, rename_site was rejected so a rename is retyping the label in each department, and no report groups by site except by matching text.
problems.fix: A client convention plus one server rule: the Departments page offers the existing site names, and save_department trims the label and refuses one that differs from an existing site only by case or whitespace.

problems.scenario: 16. Creating a PFT lab from settings
problems.detail: save_department('PFT lab', type ?) is the first step and the design does not name a core type for a department that only serves requests: laboratory and imaging belong to packs (require_pack), clinic and reception are core, and the 'general' key was rejected because it collides with two screen names. Without a type the row cannot be saved. After that it is rows: save_service(PFT lab, code loinc:19876-2 …, 'Spirometry', reply_type values, fields FEV1 (L), FVC (L), FEV1/FVC (%)) passes the 'values need fields' check; predicted values are patient-specific so reference columns stay NULL and flags stay NULL, which spec 01 allows; served_departments left empty because it is the sole provider; the request queue exists because the department has a live service; clinicians request it like any test and the technician replies with write_result from the core general request-queue screen. No pack, no deploy.
problems.fix: Name one core department type for request-only departments, for example key 'service' (a liked word: 'the PFT lab is a service department'), whose screen is the general request queue.

problems.scenario: 18. Importing an 800-test coded catalogue
problems.detail: import_services was rejected, so the client loops save_service 800 times (each with its fields), 800 settings_changes rows, each call gated by manage:services with MFA once per session; at ~50 ms a call it is under a minute. The same two gaps as scenario 2 bite harder here: (a) a failure at row 400 leaves half a catalogue, and only client-minted ids make the re-run safe; (b) 800 'loinc:' codes must exist as global codes rows with unit and kind set once, and nothing says who writes them. If the importer is allowed to create them, this organization's units become the law for every other organization on the database (a code with unit g/L blocks a later practice's g/dL, and vice versa), which is a cross-organization effect with no audit; the local: plus replaced_by_code mapping requires the same unit, so the later practice cannot even map. (c) save_service must check codes.organization_id IS NULL OR = the caller's organization, or one practice's local code can be referenced by another. Duplicates within the catalogue (two rows with one code) hit the second-provider prompt 800 times instead of a duplicate refusal.
problems.fix: Same rules as scenario 2 (client-minted ids; global codes only from migrations; UNIQUE (organization_id, department_id, code) WHERE retired_at IS NULL), plus save_service refusing a code whose organization_id is another organization's; the importer mints local: codes for anything the migration did not seed.

problems.scenario: 19. Switching a pack off while a department of its type exists (and holds are pending)
problems.detail: retire_organization_pack(org, 'laboratory') sets organization_packs.retired_at. The Laboratory department (type laboratory) stays with its 4 open requests; save_department of that type is now refused by require_pack; laboratory_mark_collected is refused; core write_result and mark_step still work, so the requests finish and the client must show the core request-queue screen for a type whose pack is off (a client rule, unstated). Billing is where it breaks. write_entry checks organization_packs at write time and inserts pack_calls rows; a request sent one second before the switch-off has a pending row. The runner's row selection has no stated join on organization_packs, so the next tick sets acting_user to pack:billing, calls billing.after_write, and mark_step(id, 'sent', 'held') succeeds after the practice switched Billing off, typically because Billing was misbehaving. The practice has no Billing screen any more, core has no 'release hold' screen, and the request sits at held until someone finds core mark_step. Test B6 ('switching Billing off leaves no request held by it') cannot pass reliably as written, and the pack-off duty ('core releases holds whose latest held step has actor_id = the pack's user') is implied but not stated.
problems.fix: Two lines in core: the runner selects pack_calls rows only where organization_packs for that (organization_id, pack) is on, and retire_organization_pack deletes that organization's pending pack_calls rows for the pack and moves every request whose latest 'held' step has actor_id = the pack's 'pack:<pack>' user from held to sent through change_request, with the admin as actor.

problems.scenario: 20. Two admins editing the same service at once
problems.detail: save_service takes the whole row plus its fields ('loaded and saved whole', like templates). Admin A loads CBC at 09:00, adds field MCHC and saves at 09:05; admin B loaded at 08:58, changes the Hb reference range and saves at 09:06. B's payload has no MCHC, so the whole-set save retires A's new field a minute after it was made, and both changes are recorded in settings_changes. No corruption, nothing crosses organizations, history is untouched, but a settings change disappears silently, and in the other order B's range change vanishes, which is the one settings change that affects flags for every result from then on. Per-row compare-and-set was rejected as 'not needed at any hospital size'; at two admins it is already possible.
problems.fix: One argument, no table: save_… takes the settings_changes id (or changed_at) the client loaded and raises changed_since_read when the row has a newer change; the client reloads and shows the other admin's change.

problems.scenario: 21. The runner reads the record on behalf of a pack (record_reads and record_not_open)
problems.detail: Amendment 7 says read_record inserts the record_reads row and every other record read raises record_not_open without a recent one (12 hours). The runner acts as the 'pack:<pack>' users row. A Billing after_write that only uses its entry argument and its own tables never reads and is fine. An after_write that calls read_entries or read_values (Imaging voiding by prior entry, Pharmacy stock by prior dispenses) raises record_not_open on every call, so tries reaches five and the row is parked; Retry parks it again. If the pack instead calls read_record first, the machine user inserts a record_reads row for every patient it touches, and the read audit fills with machine reads that hide the human ones the audit exists for. None of B1 to B14 exercises a reading after_write.
problems.fix: One rule: record_not_open and the record_reads insert apply only to users of kind staff, patient and proxy; machine and importer users read without opening and without an audit row.

problems.scenario: 22. erase_patient with pending pack_calls rows
problems.detail: erase_patient deletes everything where patient_id is in the record. pack_calls (pack, entry_id, organization_id, recorded_at, tries, tried_at, error_text) has no patient_id and no foreign key to entries, so the patient's pending rows survive the erase. The runner then loads the entry 'as it is at call time', finds none, and the design does not say what happens: a raise means five tries, then a parked row with Retry on the Organization page that names an erased entry id for ever; a silent skip would be right but is unstated. Deleting the rows inside erase_patient needs a join through entries before the entries go, which is easy but must be said because erase's WHERE is otherwise 'patient_id = X'.
problems.fix: A rule in the runner: a pack_calls row whose entry no longer exists is deleted without a call; and erase_patient deletes the patient's pack_calls rows (joined through entries) before deleting the entries.

problems.scenario: A pack function sets `opencare.acting_user_id` and acts as a doctor (impersonation through the runner's identity GUC)
problems.detail: Tick: pg_cron → runner procedure (session_user = pack_runner, or postgres on Supabase) → `set_config('opencare.acting_user_id', <organization A's 'pack:billing' users.id>, true)` → `billing.after_write(entry)`, SECURITY DEFINER owned by pack_billing, so current_user = pack_billing inside. The body does `PERFORM set_config('opencare.acting_user_id', '<Dr Smith users.id>', true); PERFORM public.write_prescription(...)`. `set_config` is callable by every role; the pack has EXECUTE on the public write_ functions and on core.write_entry. `write_prescription` → `require_access(A, 'write:prescription', patient, department)` → `current_user_id()`: session_user is not `authenticator`, so it honours the GUC and returns Dr Smith, who holds the action → an entry is inserted with author_id = Dr Smith, source = staff. Nothing catches it: B7 tests table privileges (none used), B8 tests ownership (correct), B9 tests doors (the pack used its granted door), B10 scans only core bodies and `update_` bodies, not `after_write`. The same trick lets one pack act as another pack's machine user. The design's sentence 'so no client can impersonate it' is true; the threat model omitted the pack itself, which runs on the trusted side of the guard.
problems.fix: Two lines. (1) `current_user_id()` honours the GUC only when `session_user = 'pack_runner'` AND the named users row has `kind = 'pack'` — staff impersonation becomes impossible at runtime; a pack can at most act as another pack's machine user. (2) B10 extends to every function owned by a `pack_%` role: no `set_config(`, no `SET `, no `opencare.` in the body, closing cross-pack impersonation at merge. Add to B7: `pack_%` roles hold no EXECUTE on the runner's helpers (`core.take_pack_call` etc.). The principled alternative — public functions as SECURITY INVOKER shims that capture `current_user`/`auth.uid()` and pass the caller into the private definer, no GUC at all — is cleaner but amends spec 01 invariant 14.

problems.scenario: A pack ships an updater or after_write as SECURITY INVOKER (the CREATE FUNCTION default) and runs with the caller's privileges
problems.detail: Migration `…_billing_….sql` creates `billing.update_charges(entry)` without the SECURITY DEFINER keyword and does `ALTER FUNCTION … OWNER TO pack_billing`. B8 passes (owner is the pack role). Doctor saves a billing-typed entry → `core.write_entry` (SECURITY DEFINER, owned by the core owner) → `EXECUTE format('%I.%I', 'billing', 'update_charges')`. A SECURITY INVOKER function runs as the current user at call time, which inside the definer is the core owner — so the updater has SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on every core table: `UPDATE core.requests SET step='done'`, `INSERT INTO core.user_roles`, `UPDATE core.entries SET replaced_by_id` (the trigger allows NULL → value once) all succeed. Via the runner it is worse: if pg_cron runs the tick as postgres, an invoker `after_write` runs as postgres. B7 asserts the pack *role* has no privileges — true and irrelevant, because the pack role is never the executing role. 'Inside it, current_user is the pack role and every grant applies' holds only for definer functions, and the design never says every pack function must be one.
problems.fix: B8 gains: every function owned by a `pack_%` role has `pg_proc.prosecdef = true` and `proconfig` pins `search_path`. Runtime belt at the two dispatch sites (updater in `write_entry`, after_write in the runner): one catalog read — `SELECT prosecdef AND proowner = ('pack_'||pack)::regrole FROM pg_proc WHERE oid = to_regprocedure(...)` — and refuse otherwise (a pack-type write fails, the documented limit; a pack_calls row is parked with `error_text`). Amendment 2 wording: 'every function a pack ships is SECURITY DEFINER owned by `pack_<key>`'.

problems.scenario: A pack takes core's patient advisory lock inside after_write and stalls the clinician's save
problems.detail: `write_entry` and `change_request` step 2: `pg_advisory_xact_lock(coalesce(merged_into_id, patient_id))` (spec 01 invariant 9). `pg_advisory_xact_lock` is in pg_catalog with EXECUTE to PUBLIC and needs no table privilege, so 'a pack cannot even lock a core row' is true for row locks and false for the one lock the write actually waits on. `billing.after_write`: `PERFORM pg_advisory_xact_lock(<same key derivation, read from the in-repo core source>); PERFORM pg_sleep(4)`. The runner holds it up to its statement_timeout; the doctor's `write_note` for that patient blocks at step 2; under B1's `statement_timeout = '1s'` it is cancelled. The runner retries the row five times, and a hostile pack raises after sleeping so the row stays pending — the patient is unsaveable for minutes. B1's three hostile fixtures (FOR UPDATE on own rows, raise loop, wait on own table lock) do not include this, so B1 passes while the promise is false. B7 cannot see it (no table involved).
problems.fix: Migration one: `REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION pg_catalog.pg_advisory_xact_lock(bigint), pg_advisory_xact_lock(int,int), pg_advisory_lock(bigint), pg_advisory_lock(int,int), pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared(...), pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(...), pg_try_advisory_lock(...) FROM PUBLIC; GRANT … TO <core owner>` (about ten signatures; pg_dump preserves changed initial privileges). B1 gains a fourth hostile fixture that takes the patient lock and sleeps; B9 asserts `has_function_privilege('pack_billing','pg_catalog.pg_advisory_xact_lock(bigint)','EXECUTE')` is false. Belt: the B10 pack-body scan bans `pg_advisory`.

problems.scenario: The service-role key in the invite Edge Function re-links a login: account takeover through `link_login`
problems.detail: `service_role` may execute exactly `create_organization` and `link_login`. The invite flow needs an Edge Function holding the service key: input `{users_id, email}` → `auth.admin.inviteUserByEmail(email)` → `link_login(users_id, new_auth_uid)`. Any authenticated user (a receptionist, no `manage:` action) posts `{users_id: <owner's users.id>, email: attacker@x}`. If the Edge Function checks 'is the caller logged in' but not 'does the caller hold manage:users in this organization through the database', or if `link_login` overwrites an existing `login_id`, the owner's users row now points at the attacker's auth user; `current_user_id()` returns the owner; every gate passes; MFA is per auth user so the attacker enrols their own factor and gains `manage:` too. The database cannot see any of this: `link_login` is service_role, `session_user = authenticator`, no `require_access` runs. The same door is open to `save_user` if it ever accepts `login_id` as a field (a `manage:users` holder re-points Dr X's row at their own login and writes prescriptions as Dr X).
problems.fix: (1) `link_login` sets `users.login_id` only when it is NULL and raises `already_linked` otherwise; `UNIQUE (organization_id, login_id)`; `save_user` never takes `login_id`. (2) The Edge Function calls `public.invite_user(organization_id, …)` with the caller's own JWT first (gated by `require_access(…, 'manage:users', NULL, department)`; it creates the users row with `invited_by_id`, `invited_at` and returns its id), then as service_role creates the auth user and calls `link_login` with that returned id — the service key never touches a client-supplied id; `link_login` also refuses rows with `invited_at` older than one hour. (3) B9 asserts `service_role` holds EXECUTE on exactly those two functions and no privilege on any table in `core`, `public` or a pack schema; the service key lives in that one function and no other.

problems.scenario: An administrator edits a role to grant themselves an action they lack
problems.detail: Rule as confirmed: hold-it-to-grant-it applies to `manage:` actions only. Admin U holds a custom role R = {manage:users, manage:roles}. Path A: `save_role(R, actions + 'manage:packs')` → refused, U lacks `manage:packs`. Path B: `save_role(R, actions + 'write:prescription')` → allowed (clinical), U is assigned R → U now prescribes; `settings_changes` records it but nothing refuses it. Path C: `save_user(U, roles + <built-in owner role>)` — does assigning a role count as granting its actions? The design says the rule is 'nobody may grant an action they do not hold' but names only the role editor; if `save_user` does not evaluate the target role's `manage:` actions, U assigns themselves the owner role in one call. Path D: a department-scoped granter (manage:users in Laboratory only) creates a `user_roles` row with `department_id = NULL` (everywhere) or another department — nothing in the draft scopes the grant to the granter's own scope. Path E: `save_role` on a built-in role (`organization_id IS NULL`): the gate 'resolves the organization from the row being touched' and finds NULL; unless it raises here, the edit changes rights in every organization.
problems.fix: One rule stated at both `save_role` and `save_user`: a caller may not change their own rights — not their own `user_roles` rows, not the `role_actions` of a role they hold — and may grant `manage:` actions (by role edit or by assignment) only if they hold them, in a scope no wider than their own (`user_roles.department_id` NULL requires a NULL-scoped grant). `save_role` refuses `organization_id IS NULL` (built-in roles are read-only; copy to edit). Test: an owner of A calls `save_role` with every built-in role id and with their own role; every call raises.

problems.scenario: An administrator removes their own administrator role
problems.detail: `save_user(U, roles − R)` where U is the caller and R carries `manage:users`. Under the draft the call passes `require_access(org, 'manage:users', NULL, NULL)` (U still holds it at the start), deletes the `user_roles` row, records `settings_changes`. U is now locked out of settings, and if U was the only holder the organization has no administrator (see next scenario). The self-change rule from the previous scenario closes the door; a second administrator removes U's role instead, which is the attributable, two-person path.
problems.fix: The same self-change rule: `save_user` raises `cannot_change_own_roles` when `user_id = current_user_id()`. No schema.

problems.scenario: Retiring the last administrator, including two administrators retiring each other concurrently
problems.detail: Two owners A1, A2 hold the built-in owner role. A1 calls `save_user(A2, retired_at := now())`, A2 calls `save_user(A1, retired_at := now())` in parallel. A 'last holder' check written as `EXISTS (users u JOIN user_roles JOIN role_actions WHERE action = 'manage:users' AND u.retired_at IS NULL AND u.id <> target)` sees the other row live in both transactions (READ COMMITTED) → both commit → zero administrators. The same hole exists in `retire_role` (retiring the only role carrying `manage:users`) and in `save_user` removing the last assignment. Recovery is only the Supabase dashboard as postgres, outside `settings_changes`. Also a user invited but never linked (`login_id IS NULL`) or MFA-unenrolled would count as an administrator on paper but cannot act.
problems.fix: `save_user` and `retire_role` take `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(organization_id::text))` first (the organization-level twin of the patient lock), then refuse with `last_administrator` when, after the change, no live user with `login_id IS NOT NULL` holds both `manage:users` and `manage:roles` with `department_id IS NULL`. Test: the concurrent mutual retire leaves exactly one owner.

problems.scenario: Staff of organization A call write_/read_/mark_/save_ functions with organization B's ids in every id parameter, not just patient_id
problems.detail: Caught by the gate or spec 01's composite FKs: `patient_id` (users row of the caller must be in the patient's organization); `service_id` (`entries (organization_id, service_id) → services`); `visit_id` (`(patient_id, visit_id)`); `reply_to_id`, `replaces_id`, `written_with_id` (closed-record check, same patient); `to_department_id` (`requests (organization_id, to_department_id) → departments`); `entry_id`/`request_id` (organization resolved from the row); `read_queue(department_id)` (row's organization). Not caught by anything stated: `mark_routing(assignee_id := B's user)` — no FK, the assignee's name is copied into `data.assignee_name` and shown in A (a name leak) and B's user can never see it; `responsible_id` of B's user depends on the 'X may write T' check being evaluated in A; `save_service(department_id := B's department)` is refused only at request time by the requests FK, not at settings time as promised; `served_departments`, `templates.department_id`, `user_roles.department_id`, `user_roles.role_id` (A's admin assigns B's custom role; B's admin later edits it and changes A's user's rights), `service_fields.code` naming B's `local:` code (its name is copied into A's entries), `entries.department_id` has no composite FK at all; array parameters (`laboratory_mark_collected(request_ids[])`) with one foreign element among valid ones. Spec 01 test 21 says 'every public function with A's fixture ids' but is written as one call per function, not one per parameter.
problems.fix: Composite tenant FKs, the pattern spec 01 already uses: `entries (organization_id, department_id)`, `entries (organization_id, author_id)`, `entries (organization_id, responsible_id)`, `requests (organization_id, assignee_id)`, `request_steps` via `(organization_id, actor_id)`, `services (organization_id, department_id)`, `served_departments`, `templates`, `user_roles (organization_id, department_id)` and `user_roles (organization_id, role_id)` with `roles.organization_id IS NULL` allowed by a CHECK-via-function (built-in roles); `UNIQUE (organization_id, id)` on users, departments, roles to carry them. `save_service`/`save_user` check at save time. Test 21 becomes a matrix: for each public function, for each id parameter (array elements included), substitute B's id of the same kind, expect a raise.

problems.scenario: A retired staff member holds a live JWT
problems.detail: `save_user(U, retired_at)` → next call from U's JWT (valid up to one hour): `require_access` → `current_user_id()` → `users WHERE login_id = auth.uid() AND organization_id = $1 AND retired_at IS NULL` → none → raise. Every function starts with the gate, so the record is closed on the next call. Two side doors remain: (1) Realtime — U's open socket on `record:<patient>` and `queue:<department>` keeps receiving `{entry_id}` signals until the token expires; the payload is only an id, but 'activity on patient P' is still a fact about a patient; (2) Storage — a signed URL for an `entry_files` object minted before retirement downloads until it expires. `auth.sessions` cannot be revoked from a function (that needs supabase_auth_admin).
problems.fix: Signals go on private channels with one RLS policy on `realtime.messages`: the membership InitPlan spec 01 already names (`users.login_id = auth.uid() AND retired_at IS NULL AND organization_id = <channel's organization>`), so a retired socket receives nothing. Signed URLs are minted only by `read_entry_file(entry_id, position)` (gated) with a 60-second life. JWT lifetime stays at one hour; nothing else needed.

problems.scenario: Action manifest drift between code and database
problems.detail: 'Actions come from one manifest' names no home. If the manifest is a TypeScript file and `role_actions.action` is free text: (a) a function passes `'write:vital'` (typo) to `require_access` → nobody holds it → every call fails closed — safe but silent; (b) the role editor saves an action the database never checks → a grant that means nothing; (c) removing an action from the manifest leaves `role_actions` rows that still authorise it; (d) a pack action for a pack that is off (`mark:held` with Billing off) is still grantable and, unless the gate also runs `require_pack` for pack actions, still effective. No test in B1–B14 or spec 01 covers the manifest.
problems.fix: The manifest is a table: `actions (key pk CHECK (key ~ '^(write|mark|read|manage):[a-z_]+$'), pack null → packs.key)`, shipped by migrations; `role_actions.action → actions.key ON DELETE RESTRICT`; `require_access` raises `unknown_action` when the key is absent and runs `require_pack` when `actions.pack` is set. CI: the TypeScript `Action` union is generated from `SELECT key FROM actions` and diffed; a static scan asserts every `'<verb>:<noun>'` literal passed to `require_access` in any function body exists in the table.

problems.scenario: A pack defines an action that collides with a core action
problems.detail: With `actions.key` as primary key, `INSERT INTO actions VALUES ('write:note','billing')` in a pack migration fails the migration — good — unless the migration writes `ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET pack = 'billing'`, which turns a core action into a pack action gated by `require_pack('billing')`: switch Billing off and no one can write a note. B11 ('core's catalog hash unchanged except rows in the named registries') exempts registry rows, so a content change to a core row passes. The same applies to `entry_types`, `packs`, `department_types` and `request_step` enum values.
problems.fix: A rule with a scan: a `<timestamp>_<pack>_…sql` file may not contain `ON CONFLICT`, and every registry row it inserts carries `pack = '<that pack>'` (extend B14's file check). B11 compares core registry rows by content, not count, after all pack migrations.

problems.scenario: An invitation link forwarded to the wrong person
problems.detail: 'The users row is the invitation and `link_login` links it at invite time': the admin creates the users row for Dr Okafor, the Edge Function creates the auth user and links it, GoTrue mails a magic link. Dr Okafor forwards it (or the mailbox is shared); the forwardee clicks first, sets a password and is Dr Okafor to every gate — author_id, request_steps.actor_id, record_reads all say Okafor. The link proves control of the mailbox at one moment, nothing more; no database check can tell the two people apart. What the design has: the link is single-use; `manage:` needs MFA. What it lacks: a stated link lifetime, a visible 'accepted at', and a guarantee that a second click cannot re-link.
problems.fix: Set the invite lifetime to one hour; `link_login` sets `login_id` once (see the service-role scenario) so a second acceptance cannot re-point the row; the users row carries `invited_at` and `accepted_at`, shown on the Staff page next to last sign-in, and `settings_changes` records the acceptance; an administrator retires and re-invites on doubt. Nothing more is possible without in-person verification, which is a practice rule.

problems.scenario: A compromised machine account (analyser login)
problems.detail: Machine users row `kind = 'machine'`, linked login, `user_roles` with `write:result` in the Laboratory department. `write_result(organization_id, patient_id, department := Laboratory, reply_to_id, data)` → gate passes for any patient in the organization, because staff-side gates are department- not patient-scoped, and 'results without a request need no setup' means `reply_to_id` may be NULL. So the compromised key can file a fabricated critical potassium on any of the organization's patients, source = machine, flagged, landing in the review loop where clinicians act on it; `source_key` uniqueness stops replays, not fabrication. It cannot strike, correct, read or route (no such actions), and cannot reach other organizations. Retiring the users row closes it on the next call, but discovery is the problem.
problems.fix: One rule in `write_entry` keyed on `users.kind = 'machine'`: the entry must be a reply (`reply_to_id IS NOT NULL`) to an open request whose `to_department_id` is the department the machine holds its action in; and `save_user` refuses any `read:`, `mark:` or `manage:` action, or a NULL-scoped role, for a machine user. That confines a stolen key to open requests already sent to that lab. B-test: a machine fixture writing a non-reply result raises.

problems.scenario: A patient-portal user calls staff functions
problems.detail: Today: a users row with `kind = 'patient'` has no `user_roles`; every `require_access` raises, including `read_record` on their own record, so nothing leaks and nothing works until the portal ships `patient_access`. The awkward part is what an administrator can do meanwhile: `save_user` can assign a staff role to a patient-kind user (nothing in the draft says otherwise), after which the patient reads every record in the organization through the ordinary gate. The CHECK `department_id IS NOT NULL OR source IN ('patient','import')` protects entries, not access.
problems.fix: A rule now, before the portal: `user_roles` rows exist only for `kind IN ('staff','machine','pack')`; `save_user` refuses roles for `patient`/`proxy` (one predicate, or a trigger on `user_roles` joining `users.kind`). When the portal comes, its gate clause is `patient_access (user_id, patient_id)` plus a fixed action list, never `user_roles`.

problems.scenario: SECURITY DEFINER functions with an unsafe search_path, plus CREATE and TEMP on the roles that call them
problems.detail: Spec 01 invariant 14: every *public* function is `security definer set search_path = ''`. Pack functions in `<pack>` schemas (`after_write`, `update_<list>`, mark functions) are not public and the rule does not name them. A pack definer function without `SET search_path` inherits the caller's path: from the runner, the pg_cron session's `"$user", public`; from `write_entry`, the empty path. `pg_temp` is searched first for relations whenever it is not listed, even with an empty path, so a role with TEMP privilege that reaches an unqualified name in a definer body shadows it. Supabase's defaults matter here: `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE postgres IN SCHEMA public GRANT … ON FUNCTIONS TO anon, authenticated, service_role` auto-grants every new public function to `anon`, and CREATE/TEMP for those roles are whatever the image ships. B9 would catch the anon grant in CI (same image) but only after the fact.
problems.fix: Migration one: `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE postgres IN SCHEMA public REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS FROM anon, authenticated, service_role`; `REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, service_role`; `REVOKE TEMP ON DATABASE postgres FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, service_role, pack_runner` and from every `pack_%`. Amendment 9 and B8/B9 say 'every function in `core`, `public` and every pack schema has `proconfig` pinning `search_path` (empty, or `pg_catalog`)'; B9 asserts `has_schema_privilege(role,'public','CREATE')` and `has_database_privilege(role, current_database(), 'TEMP')` are false for those roles.

problems.scenario: The private funnels `core.write_entry` and `core.change_request` are granted to packs but do not gate themselves
problems.detail: Spec 01 puts `require_access` and `require_pack` in the public wrapper and calls `write_entry` private. Spec 02 grants `pack_%` EXECUTE on `core.write_entry` and `core.change_request` so pack wrappers can end in them. Two consequences. (1) A pack wrapper that forgets the gate (`public.laboratory_write_culture` without `require_access`) is a fully ungated write of a lab type for any patient by any authenticated user; B12's hostile pack raises on purpose and does not test this omission. (2) `billing.after_write` can call `core.write_entry(type := 'note', patient := any, …)` or `core.change_request(request, step := 'done')` directly; 'a pack may never close a request with its own step' is then a sentence, since the pack machine user needs no `mark:done` to reach the private function. Invariant 11 stops pack *enum values* from closing a request, not a pack passing `done`.
problems.fix: The funnels gate themselves: `core.write_entry` runs `require_access(organization_id, 'write:' || type, patient_id, department_id)` and `require_pack(organization_id, entry_types.pack)`; the step-changing path of `core.change_request` runs `require_access(…, 'mark:' || step, patient_id, requests.to_department_id)`, while the reply fold passes no step and is not reachable with one. Wrapper gates remain as the first, cheap refusal. B12 gains a hostile wrapper with no gate: the funnel refuses it. The pack machine user's built-in role holds `mark:held` only.

problems.scenario: A pack disables the runner's statement_timeout from inside after_write
problems.detail: `statement_timeout` is a USERSET parameter; any role may `SET LOCAL statement_timeout = 0` inside a function, including a SECURITY DEFINER one owned by `pack_billing`, and the setting outlives the function's own `proconfig`. `billing.after_write`: `SET LOCAL statement_timeout = 0; PERFORM pg_sleep(1e9)`. The tick never ends, `query_canceled` never fires, and since pg_cron never overlaps runs of one job, every pack for every organization stops; charges and holds stop with it. Clinical writes are untouched (they only insert `pack_calls` rows), so this is availability of packs, not of the record. B2's poison row sleeps without touching the setting, so B2 passes.
problems.fix: The B10 pack-body scan (already needed for `set_config`) bans `statement_timeout`, `lock_timeout`, `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` in any pack function. Runtime belt: a second cron job every minute, `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE application_name = 'pack_runner' AND state_change < now() - interval '2 minutes'`; the runner sets `application_name` at start. The killed row's `tries` is already committed, so the parking logic is unchanged.

problems.scenario: A pack's public wrapper leaks across organizations because pack tables are outside core's tenant checks
problems.detail: `billing.charges (organization_id, entry_id, patient_id, …)` holds ids with no foreign key (by spec 01 design, so `erase_patient` is never blocked). `public.billing_read_charges(organization_id, patient_id)` owned by pack_billing: if it calls `require_access(organization_id, 'read:charges', patient_id, NULL)` the gate refuses a mixed pair (patient of A, organization B). If a pack wrapper takes a `charge_id` or `invoice_id` alone and resolves nothing, or gates and then queries by `patient_id` without `organization_id`, B's cashier reads A's charges. Core cannot enforce this — the table is invisible to it — so the guarantee is pack discipline plus the cross-organization test. Spec 01 test 21 says 'every public function', which includes pack wrappers only if the runner enumerates `pg_proc` rather than a hand-kept list.
problems.fix: Test 21 (and its per-parameter matrix) enumerates `SELECT proname FROM pg_proc WHERE pronamespace = 'public'::regnamespace` at run time, so every new pack wrapper is covered on the day it is added; each pack table carries `organization_id` and every pack read function resolves its organization from the row it touches, the same sentence spec 01 uses for core.

problems.scenario: A malicious pack exfiltrates the record over the network from after_write
problems.detail: `billing.after_write` holds EXECUTE on `read_record`/`read_entries` and, acting as the pack user, can read every patient in the organization the row belongs to. Exfiltration needs an outbound door: `net.http_post` (pg_net), `dblink`, `COPY … TO PROGRAM`, `pg_read_file`, or `pg_write_server_files`. On Supabase, `net` and `extensions` are granted to postgres/anon/authenticated/service_role/supabase_functions_admin, not PUBLIC, so `pack_billing` (NOLOGIN, member of nothing) has no USAGE on `net` and the call fails — but only because of Supabase's grants, which B9 does not name. B9 as written ('no function in any schema executable by PUBLIC') would fail on `pg_catalog` and `extensions`, where EXECUTE to PUBLIC is the default, so it will be narrowed in practice; it must be narrowed to the right thing.
problems.fix: B9 is scoped to `core`, `public` and pack schemas for the PUBLIC/anon assertions, and adds for `pack_%` and `pack_runner`: no USAGE on `net`, `extensions`, `vault`, `storage`, `auth`, `cron`, `realtime`, `graphql_public`; no EXECUTE on `pg_read_file`, `pg_read_binary_file`, `lo_import`, `lo_export`, `dblink%`; no membership in `pg_read_server_files`, `pg_write_server_files`, `pg_execute_server_program`, and `pg_auth_members` has no row where a `pack_%` role is either side.

problems.scenario: Who can see and change settings, and whether every settings change is attributable — including pack settings
problems.detail: Core: `save_department`, `save_service`, `save_user`, `save_role`, `save_packs`, `save_template` each start with `require_access(organization_id, 'manage:<area>', NULL, department)` (MFA `aal2` required) and insert `settings_changes (organization_id, user_id, table_name, row_id, changes, recorded_at)` with `user_id` from `current_user_id()` — attributable. Reads of settings (pickers) are organization-wide and carry no secrets beyond staff names. The gap is the pack side: `public.billing_save_price` (owned by pack_billing) updates `billing.service_prices`; the pack role has no INSERT on any core table, so it cannot write `settings_changes`, and no funnel is granted for it (the grant list is read_…, write_entry, change_request, the gates). A price change, a 'payment first' toggle, a held-request policy — all unattributed unless each pack keeps its own audit table, which is two mechanisms and a page that shows only one. `settings_changes` also lacks the insert-only trigger spec 01 gives the record.
problems.fix: One funnel: `core.record_settings_change(organization_id, table_name, row_id, changes)` (stamps `user_id`, refuses when `current_user_id()` is NULL), EXECUTE granted to `pack_%`; the B10 pack scan asserts every pack function named `<pack>_save_%` or `<pack>_retire_%` calls it; `settings_changes` gets the same refuse-update-and-delete trigger as `entries`; `read_settings_changes(organization_id)` requires any `manage:` action.

problems.scenario: 1. A pack function sleeps 5 seconds during a doctor's save
problems.detail: After-write half: `write_entry` step 7 now inserts one `pack_calls` row per pack that is on and `is_called_after_write`; `<pack>.after_write` runs only in the pg_cron runner's own transaction. A `pg_sleep(5)` there delays the runner tick, never the save. B1 and B2 prove it. Holds by construction. Updater half: `write_entry` step 6 still dispatches `format('%I.%I', entry_types.pack, 'update_'||list)` inside the write, under `pg_advisory_xact_lock(patient)`. A pack updater that sleeps 5 s (or loops) holds the patient lock for 5 s, so every concurrent core write for that patient (`write_note`, `write_vitals`) waits, and at the API role's 8 s `statement_timeout` a waiting save fails. B10 scans only `update_` bodies for `pg_sleep`/`EXECUTE`; `perform billing.helper()` where the helper sleeps passes the scan, and a plain CPU loop has no keyword at all. B12 checks that a hostile updater fails, not that it is fast. So the guarantee for the one piece of pack code left in the write is convention, and the scan is evadable.
problems.fix: B10 scans every function in a pack schema, not only `update_` bodies (same keyword list). B12 gains a sleeping updater fixture: every write of that pack's own types must finish under `statement_timeout = '1s'`, and a concurrent core write for the same patient must finish within its budget. Write the limit down next to the `write_set` one: a pack updater runs under the patient lock, so it must be O(rows) with no waits.

problems.scenario: 2. A pack takes a lock another save needs (deadlock with the patient advisory lock)
problems.detail: The runner's `after_write` may call `mark_step` → `core.change_request`, which takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock(patient)`. The xact lock is held until the runner's COMMIT. So `after_write := mark_step('sent'→'held'); perform pg_sleep(60)` or `mark_step(...); select … from billing.charges for update` (waiting on a cashier's row lock) holds the patient's advisory lock for the whole call. Every `write_entry` for that patient then waits on `pg_advisory_xact_lock`; the doctor's save fails at the API role's 8 s `statement_timeout`. The design says a `query_canceled` from 'the session timeout' ends the tick but never states the value; pg_cron sessions have none by default, and B2 passes with a 30 s timeout, which still kills an 8 s save. B1's hostile sleeper holds only 'its FOR UPDATE rows and a lock on its own table', never the patient lock, so B1 does not see this. True deadlock (runner: patient lock → billing row; cashier: billing row → patient lock) is detected after `deadlock_timeout` (1 s) and one side aborts: runner side is caught into `error_text`, cashier side retries; the doctor is only a waiter and is released. So deadlock is bounded; the sleep-or-wait-while-holding-the-patient-lock is not.
problems.fix: `ALTER ROLE pack_runner SET statement_timeout = '5s', lock_timeout = '2s'` (below the API role's 8 s), stated in the spec; B7 asserts the two settings in `pg_db_role_setting`. B1's sleeper and waiter call `mark_step` before sleeping/waiting, and the concurrent same-patient golden writes must still pass.

problems.scenario: 3. A pack function that raises on every call
problems.detail: After-write: `tries` is incremented and committed before the call, the raise is caught, `error_text` committed, loop continues; after five tries the row is parked on the Organization page. One row per (pack, entry_id), rows sink behind fresh ones. Holds. Updater: a pack `update_<list>` that raises makes writes of that pack's own types fail (B12, documented) and core writes unaffected, since dispatch is by the entry's own type. But `rebuild_record(patient_id)` replays every list for the patient in one transaction, including `<pack>.update_<list>` for that pack's old entries. One raising pack updater makes rebuild of every patient carrying one such entry fail as a whole: the core lists (`patient_medications`, `patient_problems`, `patient_allergies`) are not rebuilt, the rebuild loop of spec 01 stops on that patient, and merge (pointer + `rebuild_record`) is impossible. Spec 01 says 'updaters never raise' as a rule; nothing enforces it for a pack, and B11/B12 do not run rebuild against the hostile pack.
problems.fix: `rebuild_record` replays each list inside its own `BEGIN … EXCEPTION` block (a savepoint per list) and reports the failing list name in its per-table counts, so a raising pack list leaves that pack's rows stale and every core list rebuilt. B12 gains: rebuild of a patient holding a hostile-type entry rebuilds all core lists and reports the hostile list as failed.

problems.scenario: 4. A pack removed from the codebase but still registered
problems.detail: Migrations never leave the flat folder, so `billing` schema, `billing.after_write`, `billing.update_*` and its `entry_types` rows stay in every database; `packs.is_called_after_write` stays true; `organization_packs` rows stay on. `write_entry` keeps inserting `pack_calls` rows, the runner keeps calling `billing.after_write`, entries render from `display_line` (B13 with the client pack list emptied). Nothing breaks. If a release ships `DROP SCHEMA billing CASCADE`: B8 catches a missing `after_write` only while the flag is true, and catches a missing `update_<list>` only if it iterates retired `entry_types` rows too (it says 'every update_<list> named by a pack type', which reads as live types). A correction of a ten-year-old billing entry dispatches `billing.update_charges`, and rebuild of that patient does too. `packs.retired_at` was rejected, so there is no global 'this pack is gone' state; every organization must switch it off one by one, and a still-on organization keeps producing `pack_calls` rows that raise 'function does not exist' and park.
problems.fix: One written rule: a pack schema and its functions are never dropped; a pack is retired by retiring its `entry_types` rows and switching it off per organization. B8 iterates `entry_types` including retired rows. `write_entry` inserts no `pack_calls` row for a pack whose `is_called_after_write` is false, so clearing the flag in the same release stops the queue.

problems.scenario: 5. A pack function renamed in a release
problems.detail: `<pack>.after_write` is the contract name; B8 fails the build if it is missing, so it cannot be renamed. `update_<list>` follows `entry_types.list`; a migration that renames the table, the function and the `list` value together passes B8, one that forgets one fails it. Public wrappers are the gap: `lab_mark_collected` → `laboratory_mark_collected` (amendment 11 does exactly this) breaks every client that still calls the old name, including the offline outbox spec 01 relies on, with a PostgREST 404 at runtime. B13 (ESLint + snapshot) does not call the database, so nothing in CI notices. Ownership on rename: `CREATE FUNCTION` under a new name in a migration run as `postgres` is owned by `postgres` unless the file says `ALTER FUNCTION … OWNER TO pack_x` or `SET ROLE`; B8 catches that.
problems.fix: A golden file of public function signatures (`pg_get_function_identity_arguments`) checked in CI that may only grow; removing a line needs a matching entry in a `removed` list with the release that dropped the last caller. No schema.

problems.scenario: 6. Two packs whose reactions must happen in order
problems.detail: By contract order cannot matter: each `after_write` is idempotent on `entry_id` and makes its own data match the entry now (B4). And it cannot matter, because a pack cannot express a dependency on another pack: `pack_billing` has no USAGE on schema `laboratory`, so Billing cannot wait for a specimen row; the only shared surface is the record. The sanctioned channel is: Laboratory writes to the record (a step with `changes {specimen_no}` or an entry) and Billing reacts to the entry. Steps produce no `pack_calls` row (only `write_entry` inserts), so 'Billing charges on collected' is not expressible; charge on `sent` and on the result entry is. The hole this opens: `after_write` holds EXECUTE on `core.write_entry`, so a pack that writes an entry of its own type from `after_write` gets a fresh `pack_calls` row for that entry, whose `after_write` writes another. Idempotency on `entry_id` does not stop it; every id is new. One buggy pack fills `entries` at one row per tick forever, and nothing in B1–B14 bounds it.
problems.fix: One condition in the `pack_calls` insert: skip pack P when `current_user_id()` is P's own machine user (a pack is never told about its own writes). Say in the spec that a pack reacts to entries only, never to steps; a step a pack must react to is written as a reply entry.

problems.scenario: 8. The payment-hold race: the lab collects before Billing has placed the hold
problems.detail: Send commits, `pack_calls` row inserted, runner tick calls `billing.after_write` which does `mark_step(request_id, 'sent', 'held')`. Both `laboratory_mark_collected` and the hold go through `change_request`, which takes the patient advisory lock, so the two compare-and-sets are serialized and exactly one wins. Lab first: step is `collected`, the hold's `from_step = 'sent'` fails, Billing records 'started before payment' on its side, does not raise, the charge exists unpaid (B6). Billing first: step is `held`, `laboratory_mark_collected` fails its `from_step = 'sent'`; `billing_mark_paid` does `held → sent`, the only legal way into `sent` (amendment 8). `held` is a `request_steps` row with the machine user as actor, so rebuild folds it and `status` stays open. The window is the tick interval plus queue depth; section i accepts it. The awkward part: the spec now promises 'a few seconds after it is sent' but never names the interval, and pg_cron's default granularity is one minute; sub-minute schedules need pg_cron 1.5+. With five poison rows in front, holds trail by up to five cancelled ticks.
problems.fix: Name the interval in the spec (`cron.schedule('pack_runner', '5 seconds', …)`, pg_cron ≥ 1.5, verified in migration one) and make B6 assert that with an idle runner the hold lands within 10 s of the send.

problems.scenario: 9. Billing's reaction failing silently for a day
problems.detail: Nothing is lost: a `pack_calls` row exists per (billing, entry) until `after_write` succeeds, so a day of failures is a day of parked rows with `error_text`, each retried five times, then shown on the Organization page with Retry. After the fix ships, Retry re-runs `after_write`, which is idempotent and reads the entry as it is now, so replaced entries are voided correctly; holds mostly fail their compare-and-set by then and become 'started before payment' with an unpaid charge, the accepted exposure. Three awkward things. (1) Five tries at a 5 s tick is 25 s of patience, which contradicts the contract's own legitimate raise ('what it depends on is not there yet'): a service saved without a price parks in under a minute. (2) Nothing notices except a person opening the Organization page; a cashier notices only when a patient arrives with no charge. (3) 500 parked rows and a per-row Retry.
problems.fix: Back-off on the columns that already exist: the runner picks rows where `tries = 0 OR tried_at < now() - interval '1 minute' * 2^tries`, and a parked row (`tries >= 5`) is still retried hourly, so a fixed bug self-heals. `read_organization` returns the parked count so the page shows it, and `retry_pack_calls(organization_id, pack)` resets them all.

problems.scenario: 10. A pack writing directly to a core table
problems.detail: For `after_write` it holds: the function is `security definer` owned by `pack_billing`, so inside it `current_user = pack_billing`, which has no SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on any core table (B7) and cannot even `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` a core row. For the updater it does not: the design states only that `after_write` is `security definer`. `write_entry` is a `security definer` function owned by the core owner (on Supabase, `postgres`). When it calls `billing.update_charges(entry)` and that function is `security invoker` (the default), the updater runs as `write_entry`'s owner, inside the doctor's transaction, with every core privilege: `UPDATE core.requests SET step = 'done'`, `INSERT INTO core.entries`, `UPDATE core.patients`, or `GRANT SELECT ON core.entries TO pack_billing`. B7 passes (the role itself has no privilege), B8 passes (the function is owned by the pack role), B10 passes (no banned keyword). Ownership without `prosecdef` is no boundary at all.
problems.fix: B8 asserts `pg_proc.prosecdef` and `proconfig` contains `search_path=` for every function in a pack schema and every pack-prefixed public function. Belt and braces, database-enforced: the updater dispatch in `write_entry` looks the resolved function up once and raises `updater_not_definer` unless `prosecdef`.

problems.scenario: 12. A pack needing a new department type, a new action and a Price column on the core Services page
problems.detail: Department type: a `_cardiology_` migration inserts one `department_types` row (`key, name, pack`); B11 allows registry rows; `src/packs/index.ts` maps key → screen. Rows only, holds. Action: an `actions` row `mark:collected`, one `ADD VALUE 'collected'` file, `role_actions` for the pack's built-in role; `require_access` is generic over `user_roles → role_actions`; holds. Price: `billing.service_prices (organization_id, service_id, …)` in the pack schema, no FK; the `servicesColumns` slot renders it and saves through `billing_save_service_price`. The awkward part: saving a service and its price is two RPC calls, not one transaction, and core cannot validate a pack's column. A service saved with no price is not 'caught when settings are saved'; it surfaces as `billing.after_write` raising `price_missing` on the first request, five tries, parked (or, with the scenario 9 fix, pending under back-off). The draft's promise 'configuration problems are caught at save, never when a clinician works' is kept for the clinician (the write is unaffected) but not for the cashier.
problems.fix: One rule: a pack-owned column is saved by the pack's own function after core's save returns, and the pack's read function reports missing rows so the Services page marks them; `billing.after_write` raises `price_missing`, which is the pending row, never a clinical block. No schema.

problems.scenario: 13. Upgrading a pack's own tables
problems.detail: A `<timestamp>_billing_….sql` file alters `billing.charges`; B11 proves core's catalog hash is unchanged; `CREATE OR REPLACE` keeps function owners; pending `pack_calls` rows survive the release and Retry runs the new code; a pack derived table with an updater is rebuilt by `rebuild_record`; charges and payments are never rebuilt, by design. The trap is ownership of tables. Migrations run as `postgres`. `CREATE TABLE billing.refunds` in such a file is owned by `postgres`; `pack_billing` holds ALL on the schema, which is CREATE and USAGE only, not INSERT on that table. The first `billing.after_write` that touches `billing.refunds` gets `permission denied for table refunds`, and every row parks. B8 checks functions, not relations, so the build passes.
problems.fix: Every `_<pack>_` migration begins with `SET ROLE pack_<key>;` (a superuser may set any role), so every object it creates is pack-owned; B8 asserts `pg_class.relowner` for every relation in a pack schema as it does `pg_proc.proowner`.

problems.scenario: 15. One database hosting two organizations with different packs
problems.detail: `organization_packs` is per organization; `require_pack(organization_id, pack)` refuses new entries of an off pack's types for B while A writes them; `write_entry` inserts `pack_calls` rows only for packs on for `entry.organization_id`. The runner sets `opencare.acting_user_id` to 'this organization's pack:<pack> user', so `require_access` and `request_steps.actor_id` are organization-scoped, and a buggy pack that passes an organization B request id to `mark_step` is refused because A's machine user is not a member of B. Pack tables carry `organization_id` and are filtered by the pack's own code; a pack that forgets the filter leaks its own data across organizations, which spec 01 test 21 catches for public functions but no test catches for `after_write`. Unstated: who creates the machine `users` row (`kind = 'machine'`) and its `user_roles` row for the pack's built-in role, per organization, per pack. Mandatory `switch_on` was rejected, so it must be core's duty, and until it exists the runner cannot act and every row parks.
problems.fix: One rule: `save_organization_pack` (switching a pack on) inserts the machine `users` row and its `user_roles` row for the pack's built-in role in the same transaction, and retiring the pack retires them. Test: switch a pack on for a fixture organization, send one write, and expect a processed `pack_calls` row whose `request_steps.actor_id` is that machine user.

problems.scenario: 16. A third-party pack of unknown quality
problems.detail: Same repository, so it meets B1–B14 at merge time and the grants at run time. What the tests as listed do not see, because its migration runs as `postgres`: `cron.schedule(…)` a job that runs any SQL as `postgres` every minute; `ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE core.entries`, which streams the record to any subscriber (B9 names PostgREST and pg_graphql, not Realtime); `GRANT postgres TO pack_evil` with NOINHERIT, invisible to `has_table_privilege`, then `SET ROLE postgres` inside its function; a trigger on `core.entries` or an event trigger; `ALTER ROLE authenticated SET statement_timeout = 0`; an `entry_types` row with `pack = 'billing'` so its entries run Billing's updater, which B8 accepts because `billing.update_charges` exists and is Billing-owned; `role_actions` giving its own machine user `mark:cancelled` and `write:note`, so its `after_write` can close any request in the organization. Whether B11's 'catalog hash' covers these depends on a definition the design does not give.
problems.fix: Define B11's hash as everything in `pg_catalog` outside pack schemas: `pg_proc` bodies and `proacl`, `relacl`, `nspacl`, `pg_auth_members`, `pg_db_role_setting`, `pg_trigger`, `pg_event_trigger`, `pg_policy`, `pg_publication_tables`, and `cron.job` (exactly the runner and the purge). Add: every registry row a `_<pack>_` file inserts carries that pack's key, and a pack's machine role holds only `mark:held` and actions whose type or step belongs to that pack.

problems.scenario: 17. Renaming a department type key
problems.detail: `departments.type` references `department_types.key`. The draft `department_types (key, name, pack, …)` has no `retired_at`, although spec 01 says every settings table has one and `department_types` is a settings row 'shipped by packs'. So a rename is either `UPDATE department_types SET key = …` with `ON UPDATE CASCADE`, which rewrites a key (spec 01: keys are never renamed or reused) and writes no `settings_changes` row per department, or it is impossible. History is safe either way: entries copy `department_name`, never the type key. The client's key → screen map is the only reader.
problems.fix: `department_types.retired_at`, which the spec 01 settings invariant already requires, plus the `entry_types` sentence copied over: keys are never renamed or reused; a rename is a new key row, the old one retired, and `save_department` moves each department across as one settings change.

problems.scenario: 18. Presets that reference packs the practice has not enabled
problems.detail: Presets are client data (the `presets` tables were rejected). 'Polyclinic with lab and pharmacy' creates departments of types `laboratory` and `pharmacy`, whose `department_types.pack` is `laboratory` and `pharmacy`. If the first-run order name → packs → preset left those packs off, the preset calls `save_department(type = 'laboratory')`. Nothing in the design says `save_department` checks the type's pack, so the row is saved: a department with a screen the client cannot show and services no `write_request` can send to (`require_pack` refuses the pack's types). ESLint's `no-restricted-imports` cannot see a string key `'laboratory'` inside `src/core` preset data, so B13 passes.
problems.fix: `save_department` calls `require_pack(organization_id, department_types.pack)` when the type's pack is not null (one gate line, database-enforced). Each pack contributes its preset fragments through `src/packs/index.ts`, and a CI check asserts no core preset names a department type whose `pack` is not null.

problems.scenario: 19. A pack calls the granted private funnels (`core.write_entry`, `core.change_request`) directly
problems.detail: Pack roles hold EXECUTE on `core.write_entry` and `core.change_request` because a pack's own `write_ecg` and `laboratory_mark_collected` must end in them. Spec 01 puts `require_access` in the public wrappers, not in the funnels; `write_entry` steps 1–8 contain no access check and resolve `organization_id` from the patient. So `billing.after_write`, running as `pack_billing` with A's machine user as acting user, can call `core.write_entry` for a patient of organization B, or write a core `prescription` for any patient, bypassing `write_prescription`'s validation; and `core.change_request(request_id, step => 'cancelled')` closes any request without `mark_step`'s compare-and-set, which is exactly what 'a pack may never close a request' forbids. B7 (table privileges) passes, B8 passes, B10 scans core bodies only, spec 01 test 21 exercises public functions, not the runner. `security definer` is the mechanism that makes the pack able to reach the funnel at all.
problems.fix: Two lines in the funnels, database-enforced: `write_entry` and `change_request` begin with a membership assert (the acting user is an unretired `users` row of the row's organization), and when `current_user LIKE 'pack\_%'` `write_entry` refuses a type whose `entry_types.pack` is not that pack and `change_request` refuses `done`, `cancelled` and `reopened`. B7 gains a hostile `after_write` that tries all three.

problems.scenario: 20. The entry is gone before the tick (erased, or its patient merged) and the runner cannot read `entries`
problems.detail: The runner calls `<pack>.after_write(entry)` 'with the entry as it is at call time', but B7 requires that `pack_runner` cannot SELECT from `entries`. So the runner must fetch the row through a core `security definer` function (`core.next_pack_call()` returning the entry and locking the row), which the design implies but does not name. When the entry is gone (`erase_patient` ran between the write and the tick) that function returns no entry; `after_write(NULL)` would raise and park five times for a patient who no longer exists. Merge is fine: `patient_id` on the entry is literal and the pack keys by entry id. The future erase row ('a `pack_calls` row when erase is built') cannot carry a `patient_id` in the table as amended, so a pack cannot learn whom to erase; that is deferred with erase, correctly, but the row shape will need to say it.
problems.fix: Name `core.next_pack_call()` (security definer, returns the row plus the entry) as the runner's only read; when the entry no longer exists the runner deletes the `pack_calls` row and commits. Decide the erase row's shape with erase, not now.

killed: naming: Name the reception-to-clinic tie: `departments.reception_department_id` — This adds a column whose value is speculative for the first two years. The clinic has one reception, and a missing column behaves exactly like the proposed NULL: every reception may book into every clinic. Deferring it is therefore perfectly additive and needs no re-setup. The shape is also unproven. A single pointer cannot express a clinic fed by two receptions, a main desk and a floor desk. Committing to the column now risks replacing it with a table later. Keep the owner's decision as one sentence under 'written as rules now, built later'. When a second reception actually exists, choose column or table from the real case. If it is a column, `reception_department_id` is the right name.
